exact_items: Route payload continuation: all cmd.*.open_in_* and cmd.*.show_in_* commands must carry the canonical route payload schema (surface_id + object_kind + object_id + project_id + optional scoped fields)
Commands that currently use bare page: string as a destination arg must be migrated to canonical route payload

UI_Command_Catalog.md must be the SSOT for the canonical cmd.* argument shapes; any divergence in Orchestrator_Page.md, Run_Graph_View.md, or FinalGUISpec.md must be corrected by pointing to the catalog definition
OperationalIdentity block is missing from runtime snapshots in storage-plan.md and Contracts_V0.md
OperationalIdentity must carry: effective_account_id, effective_runtime_id, effective_persona_key, execution_role, actor_kind, requested_account_binding, any_pressure_flags, any_degradation_flags
This block is the single source of effective-identity truth for auditing, receipts, and downstream projections
notes: OperationalIdentity block is the single key that makes multi-actor attribution, account-switch detection, and degradation signals auditable in one lookup

exact_items: execution_role and actor_role are used interchangeably across shard content — need one canonical name
execution_role is the preferred canonical name: it distinguishes the role the actor plays during this execution (not their long-lived identity role)
actor_role must be retired; all docs that reference actor_role must be updated to execution_role
Models_System.md conflates transport host identity (the server/endpoint serving the model) with upstream provider identity (the commercial provider whose model is being called)
These are different identity axes: transport host is infrastructure; upstream provider is commercial relationship
Identity attribution for usage, billing, rate limiting, and permission scoping must separate these two axes
A request may go through a locally-hosted transport proxy but the upstream provider identity is still an external commercial entity
heading_hints: ## Transport Host vs Upstream Provider Separation
notes: This conflation causes identity contamination in usage records: a locally-proxied call looks attributed to a different entity than the actual commercial provider

exact_items: Projection-freshness trust vocabulary must be distinct from Preview trust_tier — trust_tier is already occupied in that namespace
Projection trust vocabulary must use a different name such as projection_freshness, data_freshness, or staleness_state
Using trust_tier for both preview capability trust and projection freshness would create a naming collision across surfaces
Provider_OpenCode.md maps canonical thread_id to OpenCode session ID — this is a contract bug
thread_id is a canonical conversation thread identity; OpenCode session ID is a transport artifact tied to a single process instance
These must be separate fields: canonical thread_id remains stable across reconnects; opencode_session_id is a per-connection transport artifact
notes: This bug causes conversation thread identity to break on reconnect — a direct user-facing correctness failure

exact_items: Approval Scope Key for Permissions_System.md: define the canonical scope key tuple that gates always/never approval decisions
Proposed canonical scope key: (actor_kind, tool_id, scope_context) where scope_context is (project_id, lane_id?, worktree_id?)
Always/never approvals with a session-global scope key are unsafe under multi-lane / multi-actor execution
account-health / pressure event family: account_health_event must carry at minimum: account_id, health_kind, health_level, threshold_crossed?, details
account_pressure_episode must be queryable from any surface that shows account health trends
Models_System.md must also have an account-health display section for model-provider account degradation
Identity semantics across docs must converge on OperationalIdentity block as the canonical snapshot
requested_account_id must always be accompanied by requested_account_binding (none / preferred / required) to clarify what failure mode applies when the requested account is unavailable
effective_account_id must always be present (may equal the default) and never absent from any record that involves a provider/model call
heading_hints: ## Requested vs Effective Account Binding Rules
notes: requested_account_binding semantics determine whether a mismatch triggers degraded-mode or hard-block — this is a behavioral safety requirement

exact_items: Permissions_System.md permission snapshot invalidation on account switch must be defined explicitly

Rule: when effective_account_id changes for an actor/lane, all always/never approvals scoped to that (actor, tool, scope_context) where scope_context includes account-sensitive tools must be invalidated
Account-neutral tool approvals (e.g., read-only filesystem reads) may survive account switches if explicitly exempted in the approval scope definition
heading_hints: ## Permission Snapshot Invalidation on Account Switch

exact_items: Persona resolution chain must use the canonical requested/effective identity fields (requested_persona_key, effective_persona_key) throughout Personas.md and Prompt_Pipeline.md
Persona documents still have internal references to select_for_tier() and legacy persona_override_owner_id semantics that must be replaced
Persona SSOT section in Personas.md must not violate its own canonical field naming
Bridge envelope in CLI_Bridged_Providers.md must carry: effective_account_id, execution_role, actor_kind, lane_id, worktree_id when the bridged provider is called in a multi-actor context
Bridged-provider usage events must include OperationalIdentity fields; bare bridge events without attribution are invisible to governance/audit
OpenCode SSE must be lane-filtered: events from actor A must not leak to actor B's SSE stream even in the same server process
notes: OpenCode SSE lane contamination is a data isolation and governance failure under multi-actor execution
